correctness.rationale: Conditioning on pi(i)=j gives the centered projection -2(i-(n+1)/2)(j-(n+1)/2)/(n-1). Covariance of inversion count with each displacement threshold is therefore an explicit sum over fixed diagonal separations. Direct evaluation gives the closed formula, positive on the complete integer domain. The layer-cake decomposition of every monotone penalty and strictly positive first differences yield the stated consequences. The finite verifier exhaustively independently compares rational covariances through n=8 and algebraic first differences through n=500; the proof does not depend on extrapolation.

source_inspections.title: Spearman’s Footrule as a Measure of Disarray

value.rationale: Thresholded positional displacement counts naturally retain the displacement scale lost in the classical total footrule. Proving a positive covariance for every nonconstant increasing displacement penalty supplies a robust, structural comparison of Kendall inversion discordance and a broad family of rank-error losses. The exact threshold dependence has a nontrivial interior sharp maximizer asymptotic to 0.366n, showing which displacement scale contributes the greatest covariance. This motivated profile cannot be read off from the known total-footrule covariance.
